comments.text: The prefix match is not actually case-insensitive: only the three literals "Bearer ", "bearer " and "BEARER " are handled, so mixed-case schemes like "BeArEr <token>" (valid per RFC 9110, where auth schemes are case-insensitive) are still passed through unstripped and the request is treated as unauthenticated. Use a real case-insensitive check, e.g. `if len(token) >= 7 && strings.EqualFold(token[:7], "Bearer ") { return token[7:] }`, and add tests for mixed-case variants.

Remove the code comment addressed to 'automated reviewers and code verification tools'; it is not documentation of the code and does not belong in the source. The claims in it and in the PR description are not substantiated by any added tests.
